prompt_package.goal_summary: Turn rough notes into a clean one-page infographic with exact numbers and no invented facts.

user_profile.who: Consultant or teacher who writes in bullet points

blocks.task: Design a one-page infographic titled {{title}} that explains {{topic}} to a beginner using only the facts I give you.
blocks.subject: A vertical stack of {{section_count}} numbered sections. Each section has a short heading, one sentence, and one simple icon. Section {{highlight_index}} is the visual focus and gets a filled accent panel.
blocks.scene: Flat {{background_color}} page with a slim {{brand_color}} header band at the top and a one-line footer reading {{footer}}. Generous white space between sections. No photographic elements.
blocks.camera: Straight-on flat view. The page fills the frame edge to edge with an even 6% margin. No perspective, no shadows, no mockup device.
blocks.light: Flat even color. No gradients except one soft tint inside the accent panel.

text_in_image.placement: top left, inside the header band

locks: Copy every number, date and name exactly as given. Never round, never estimate, never add a statistic.
The layout order is fixed: title, then sections top to bottom, then footer.
Icons stay simple line shapes. No faces, no flags, no logos.
avoid: text smaller than the body size
words in a language other than the one I wrote

input_schema.description: Your notes go in as short, plain sentences. Numbers must be written exactly as they should appear.

fields.name: topic
fields.example: why reply time decides whether a lead buys

fields.name: fact_1
fields.example: 78% of buyers pick the first reply

fields.name: fact_2
fields.example: A 24h delay cuts close rate by half

fields.name: fact_3
fields.example: One saved deal pays for a year of tooling

output_schema.description: Rendered page plus a verification pass.

fields.name: readability_check
fields.example: Body text legible at 50% zoom on a laptop.

example_input.title: THE 3 COSTS OF SLOW EMAIL
example_input.fact_1: 78% of buyers pick the first reply
example_input.fact_2: A 24h delay cuts close rate by half
example_input.fact_3: One saved deal pays for a year of tooling

non_obvious_insights: This model renders long text well, but each extra word competes for space. Write the on-image copy first, in the JSON, then design around it.
Put the exact strings in the JSON and nowhere else. Notes pasted into the task line get paraphrased; lines listed under text_in_image get copied.
Say 'no perspective, no shadows, no mockup device'. Otherwise you get a pretty photo of a poster instead of a flat page you can post.
A 4:5 page survives both a LinkedIn feed and a carousel swipe. Export one file, use it twice.
Section labels are the model's job; section numbers are yours. Number the sections yourself in the text strings if the order matters.
Ask for a footer source line. It costs one line and adds instant credibility.
Run a letter-by-letter audit on numbers only. Numbers are where errors become expensive.
monetization_ideas: Sell 'notes to one-pager' as a fixed-price service for coaches and consultants.
Package 12 infographics per quarter for a B2B client, priced per quarter, not per image.
Turn a client's internal report into a shareable page and charge for the design pass.
Sell the empty template plus a 30-line style guide to agencies that need on-brand consistency.
Upsell a slide version: same blocks, aspect_ratio 16:9, one run per slide.
prompt_package.reusability_notes: One package covers process diagrams, comparison tables, timelines and stat cards: change section_count, facts and the icon wording only. For 21:9 web banners, cut to two facts. For a 9:16 story, stack four short facts. Keep the locks unchanged; they are what makes the output trustworthy.
